utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we would not ask for Ambassador Arria to come back. Give me 30 seconds, please. I just want to confer with colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: There will be no re-cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much, Ms. Sellers. Ambassador -- yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I take it -- I hope it's a hundred per cent clear that no rights whatsoever are being reserved by the Prosecution. I wish merely to make this observation, Your Honour. I was careful to choose exhibits where I anticipated that because they concern an investigation into Mr. Turajlic's assassination and one sentence about Brigadier Hayes that there wouldn't be any big fuss by the Prosecution. I appreciate they're not applying to re-cross-examine now, but I don't accept any suggestion that the Prosecution were ambushed or that they had anything but the fullest rights to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would -- I would have definitely intervened and I'm sure that my colleagues would have intervened too had we smelt an ambush of any kind, but I don't think we're -- let's stop it there, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have just one question for you, and forgive my inquisitiveness. When you testified in Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: DIEGO ENRIQUE ARRIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you testified in Milosevic, were you shown these clips from the video taken -- allegedly by the UN?

utterances.speaker: DIEGO ENRIQUE ARRIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, this came 12 years later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So this is the first time you're seeing this video?

utterances.speaker: DIEGO ENRIQUE ARRIA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. That explains part of his testimony of yesterday. Ambassador, I can't tell you how grateful we are for you to have come over and give testimony. I know how busy you are, and we appreciate you coming here to give evidence as Defence witness this time. On behalf of Judge Brydensholt, Judge Eser but also on behalf of the Tribunal in general therefore, I thank you and we all wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. It's a privilege.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will now receive all the assistance you require --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's a privilege.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, Madam Vidovic, Mr. Wubben, we have got eight minutes before the break. Do you want to start now or shall we break now and resume in 30 minutes' time?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd rather we have a break and then continue after 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So we'll have a 30-minute break starting from now. That means we will start at 4.22. 4.22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Start from here. You requested earlier on, Mr. Jones, permission to file a reply to the Prosecution response in relation to Rule 68 disclosure material. We are granting you that provided what will be contained in this fresh reply is something new and not a repetition of what has been said already.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And the reply is what you have before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't have it before me, sorry. I mean, what I have before me is the reply with regard to the Rule 70 witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. Rule 68. Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Make sure that it is something new, otherwise you will have it back.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, what do you want to do? Shall we deal with this matter relating to Major Dudley? Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would really appreciate it if we could start with this witness. We are very careful when we plan the time within which we can finish this and the next two witnesses, and we would really like to finish these testimonies before the winter recess, and that is why we made sure our responses are in written form, so we lose as little time as possible in trial as possible on these matters. See I would really appreciate it if we could start with the witness who is actually waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's hear what Mr. Wubben has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to make an oral submission, as I already stated, and I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: After which I take it we will leave it at that and we will proceed with a decision later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What I suggest, Your Honour, is that by the end of this proceeding let's -- I need for myself, I think, ten minutes to 15 minutes. I don't know what the Defence need, but I like to request you permission, allowance to respond to the filing, the written filing, the reply by today. And then I have a further submission regarding the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want to respond to this further filing, yes, of course, but please do it by the end of today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have a further submission to make, let's hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It will be a short submission in addition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because our idea is that we will take it that you don't want to make further submission on both parts and we will then withdraw -- withdraw, I don't mean to say that we will stop the sitting and go to our rooms. It means that we will withdraw, deliberate, and we'll come back to a decision at the earliest opportunity after we have come to a conclusion. At the moment, of course, we are very much open to conviction from either side. Yes, Mr. Wubben, what's your new submission, the one you said in the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The one in the very beginning is related to in addition, subsequent to the response I would like to do also orally, meaning that my preference would be to deal with both, unless you ask me now to go ahead and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. No. You include everything in your reply, but make sure, please, that you file that at the earliest. I know it's already half past 4.00 but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will do it orally. I prefer to do it orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Just to expedite the proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much time will you require?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I guess 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 15 minutes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We -- in fact, as my colleague just said, we have a very tight scheduling of witnesses, and that's why we've been filing written submissions. I don't see why firstly the Prosecution doesn't simply file a written submission and that way we have -- we can save needed court time. Of course, if Mr. Wubben speaks for 15 minutes, then I have a right to rely to that because he's going to raise matters. In addition, as you may notice from the filing, we're awaiting clarification from the government in question on two other matters, and so I don't see that this will be a wonderfully efficient way of dealing with matters. I submit a written submission would be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what Mr. Wubben has to tell us. And I'm not in the mind of the US government to know what they will respond to the new questions posed by the Defence. Yes. We'll stop half an hour -- at quarter to 6.00, quarter to 6.00, to hear submissions, but that will be the end of it. That will be the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because we need our time to discuss as well. I mean, this morning I wrote two decisions in other case. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's bring in -- the witness hasn't got any protective measures, does he? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. At one point or maybe on two occasions I intend to address the Chamber with the request to move into a private session. But no, there no protective measures in respect of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I noticed at least from what I was informed today that you have revised somewhat the summary of what he will be testifying upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How does that lead us as regards time needed by the Defence for examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I try to avoid any repetitive matters, anything that has so far been testified by other witnesses, but as you have had an opportunity to see during the proofing, I was able to establish that the witness is aware of many relevant issues for this case. Eight hours, therefore. And we envisage four working days, that is until the end of this week for this witness. What we need is eight hours, and I believe it is in line with the practice that we have had so far, that is that during the examination-in-chief by the Prosecutor we had, I think, 75 to 80 per cent of that time for the -- for the cross-examination, and I believe that we will stick to that for the remainder of this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will start and we'll do our best to make sure that this witness goes home the end of this week. But basically we're saying today is already Tuesday, we have Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. That's three times three, nine, plus another hour and a half. I don't think we will finish with this witness on Friday. I don't think so. He must be put on the alert that he is going to spend the weekend here. All right. Good afternoon to you, Mr. Smajlovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am the Presiding Judge in this trial. My name is Carmel Agius, and I come from Malta. To my right is Judge Hans Henrik Brydensholt from the Kingdom of Denmark, to my left is Judge Professor Albin Eser from the Republic of Germany. We are presiding over this case against Naser Oric, and you have been summoned as a Defence witness by Mr. Oric, which means you are going to start giving evidence in a couple of minutes' time. However, before you start giving evidence, our Rules require that you make a solemn declaration; in other words, that you confirm solemnly equivalent to an oath to us and to everybody that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text is contained on a piece of paper which is going to be handed to you now. Please read it out loud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us that you will be testifying the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Please make yourself comfortable. Sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will explain to you what is going to happen. First of all, you would have noticed, sir, that I am not speaking your language. I'm speaking English, in English, and what I am saying is being translated to you in your own language or in a language which you understand. That's very important. And I want to make sure that throughout all your stay here and throughout all your testimony you are receiving interpretation in your own language at all times, and if at any time there are problems with the reception of interpretation, or if at any time the sound level is not agreeable to you, please draw our attention straight away. That happens sometimes. And we will give it all due attention and we will rectify it, but I want to make sure that you are able to follow what's being said at all times and at every given moment. All right? Secondly, you are considered by the Defence as a very important witness, and they are expecting to put questions to you for a long time, which they have a right to do. So you will have to be with us here for a few days, and in all probability we will not be able to finish with you this week. We will do our utmost and our best to do that, but I don't promise you that we will be able to finish with you this week, which basically means that you will need to stay here over the weekend. During these days, you can of course be in contact with your family, and you can make calls to other persons, provided that you do not yourself discuss or allow others to discuss or mention to you the matters related to the events with which this trial is concerned or matters related to your testimony. It would be a violation of our laws if you try to communicate with anyone while you are still here and until you have completed your testimony in chief and in cross. The other thing is this: Very much depends on how you answer questions. If you elaborate and you give more information than what the question asks from you, then you are going to be here a long time. So my recommendation to you, Mr. Smajlovic, is that you try and adopt a very simple approach in your testimony when trying to answer all the questions that are put to you, and that is answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question. If you give more information, you will be here longer. So if you can answer a question by a simple yes or no, then answer it by a simple yes or no. If you need to give explanations, look at us and we will give you a chance to explain. But if you can answer the question by a yes or a no, just answer it that way and don't go into further details. The Defence counsel, lead counsel, Madam Vidovic will go first, and what she has finished it will be Mr. Di Fazio, the gentleman who is nearer to you, that will cross-examine you on behalf of the Prosecution, but I'll address you on that when we come to the cross-examination. Madam Vidovic -- you will be here in the witness box for about an hour today, then tomorrow we will have a full day. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Smajlovic.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your name is Suad Smajlovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were born on the 4th of January, 1967 in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your father's name is Avdo; mother's name Fadila, nee Sadikovic?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You went to primary school which you finished in 1981 in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From 1985 until 1990, you worked in the Energoinvest company in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From 1990 until 1992, you were in the reserve forces of the security services centre in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did your military service in 1986 in Bela Crkva in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the transport unit?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You spent the war in the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the fall of Srebrenica, you worked as assistant commander for security of the 287th Brigade in Stupari, then in Dubrava?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1997, you were admitted into the professional service of the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina where you worked until 2004?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During this period of time, you spent some time in training under the auspices of the government of the united -- United States for the Federation army?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This included training in control and command and in manipulating various types of weapons, and also it included equating yourself with various types of weapons used by the NATO forces?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you spent some time in training in Ankare and the officers' school of NATO which was organised in Pakistan. All of this under the auspices of the government of the US.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Smajlovic, can I please ask you to make a brief pause after I finish my question so that it can be interpreted by the interpreters. Thank you. During the year of 1995 in Potocari, approximately 18 of your close relatives went missing?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're married and father of two under 8 children?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're currently employed in the company called Gama Sigurnost, which deals with the protection of people and facilities, and you are in charge, you are a manager of a sector there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Smajlovic, I'm sitting here. You can -- you can turn to me from time to time. So far we have received a lot of information. We have heard a lot of information about the events which preceded the war events in 1992 in Srebrenica and which relate to the arming of the Serb population, and that is why I am not going to ask you a lot of questions about that. I will also skip a number of details and information to which you had access as a reserve police officer, all of which was testified by several witnesses in this case, but I will limit myself to several details in relation to this topic. So while you were working as a reserve police officer, did you have any information about the existence of Serb Crisis Staffs in the early months of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you obtain that information?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: While visiting the area, the Muslim and Serb villages, but also from colleagues who were of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were all of your colleagues policemen in the Srebrenica police station, were they -- were all of them for SDA or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I ask you at this point to move into private session because of some names that the witness will mention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the usher please to show D625 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document, for the exhibit, let me state for the record that this is an instruction for the organisation and activities of the Serb people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in a state of emergency from 1991. Witness, can I please ask you to have look at page 2, item 3 of this document. Let me quote, and I kindly ask you to listen to me carefully: "The Municipal Committee of the SDS will immediately form a crisis headquarters of the Serb people in the municipality which will include all members of the secretariat of the municipal committee of the SDS. Post-holders in the municipalities, SDS nominees for the following bodies, president of the Municipal Assembly or president of the municipal Executive Board, head of the public security station, or commander of the police station, commander or head of the municipal territorial defence headquarters, secretary of the municipal Secretariat for National Defence, or another official from that secretariat who is a nominee of the SDS; "Deputies in the Assembly of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina; "Members of the Main Committee of the SDS of Bosnia-Herzegovina from that municipality." Witness, you mentioned the names of the people with whom you talked and I kindly ask you not to repeat their names. On the basis of the conversations that you had with these people, were you able to find out that post-holders in the municipality, Serbs, later became members of those Crisis Staffs, such as the president of the SDS, the head of the police station and others?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew, for instance, that Goran Zekic, the president of the SDS, was a member of the Crisis Staff, as well as the former head of the CSB, Sava Aleksic, who was the head in 1990 and who was also a member of the Serb Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "Serb Crisis Staff," can you tell us what the municipality you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: The municipality of Srebrenica. The Serb municipality of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on your knowledge about the events which happened later in Srebrenica, were members of the Srebrenica Crisis Staff, did they have a role in the events around the 17th of April, 1992, in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the 17th of April, 1992 -- rather, before that time, before the 17th of April, 1992, did you already know what was happening with the Muslim population in Eastern Bosnia in towns such as Bijeljina or Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew that, thanks to a number of reports in the police station, also through listening to the local stations, police stations, and also from the stories of that population from the people who were able to flee and come to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything? What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they spoke of horrible things that had taken place there, murders, expulsions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask for a new exhibit, Defence exhibit to be shown to the witness at this point. It is an article published in the Banja Luka based Nezavisne Novine on the 28th of November, 2005. The title of the article is "The trial" -- "The Main Trial Against Yellow Wasps Starts." While the article is being distributed, Your Honours, let me draw your attention to the first page which contains information as to the date, the time when the article was published. The article itself is on the next page. Let me quote from the article. I'm not going to quote the article in its entirety. It starts as follows: "Tuzla trial of Branko Grujic, Branko Popovic, Dragan Slavkovic, Ivan Korac, Sinisa Filipovic, and Dragutin Dragicevic accused of war crimes committed from April until June of 1992 in the area of Zvornik starts today before the War Crimes Chamber of the district court in Belgrade." Let me now quote the third and the fourth paragraphs which say: "The head of Zvornik Municipality at the time, Branko Grujic, and the commander of the TO staff in Zvornik at the time, Branko Popovic, have been accused of the forced movement of 1.822 Muslims from the villages of Kozluk and Skocic. "The indictment also covers the monstrous murders of at least 19 Muslim civilians at "Dom Kulture" in Celopek, at the "Ekonomija" farm and a place called Ciglana. Bodies of the missing inhabitants of Zvornik were found and exhumed from mass graves, Berbica mezarije, Ramin grob, Kazanbasca, and Crni Vrh where numerous evidence about the ways of liquidation of the victims was found." Let me ask you a question, Witness. It is stated here that the head of the municipality and the commander of the TO staff in Zvornik is about to stand trial for murders and expulsions of the civilian Muslim population from the area in question. I would like to know whether the information which you said you had access to at the time, is this the information that you were able to obtain from the radio and from the refugees who had come to the area of Srebrenica, that is that Muslims were being killed and expelled in the area of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was very well coordinated, very well planned, and the ethnic cleansing of the entire area had been prepared, the area where Muslims lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We will get to that, Witness. Let me first ask you something in relation to this article. You have heard the names that I just read out. Is it correct that I had shown you this article before you came here to testify?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know any of these individuals whose names I have just read out from the article?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who do you know?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Dragutin Dragicevic, Serb, from the village of Samotica near Srebrenica, who has already been convicted of heinous murders of 25 Muslims in Bijele Polje in the Republic of Serbia. And in early 1990, he had already left as a volunteer to the battlefield, and later we heard that he had committed heinous murders of Croatian Catholics in the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know this individual?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: We went to school together.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like this exhibit to be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will become Defence Exhibit D963.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the refugees who had come from Zvornik, did they tell you anything about the fact that Muslims had been given an ultimatum in Zvornik, an ultimatum to hand over the weapons?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica, around the 15th of April, 1992, did you receive an ultimatum to that effect, to surrender the weapons or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time you were given this ultimatum to surrender the weapons, the ultimatum which was issued by Serbs, did you at that point realise that the same fate was awaiting you, that is the murders, rapes and looting, everything that you had heard from the refugees who had come to your area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do? I mean you personally.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1992, I went to work as usual. I took the rifle which I had signed out for and some ammunition because I knew that I would need it. I went back to Kazani where I realised that the population was panicking, and it was decided that we would not surrender the weapons but flee to the woods instead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we show a map to the witness at this point. This map will help us with his testimony. This is a part topographical map of Zvornik of a scale of 1:100.000. That's the same map we've been using so far. Witness, the map will be placed to your side. You see where it is. Please take the pointer you have there, and I will ask the usher's assistance in giving the witness a marker, a highlighter. Please show the Trial Chamber by using the map, and you can turn to the map, please, where Kazani is on this map.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please keep the map there. We will need it at a later stage during your testimony. I will go back to the events you started relating just now. You said that you called on the people to flee to the woods there. Did they listen to what you were saying and follow suit?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many people were there with you approximately?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: About 100 women, children, and elderly people, and there were two newborn babies with us as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understood that you went to the woods on the 16th of April, 1992. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How much time did you spend with those people in the woods?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: We stayed there for about two weeks. We were outdoors without any provisions, any food, water, or shelter. At the time, the weather was so bad you had practically all the seasons alternating at the time. As the Serbs entered Srebrenica, they first started shelling --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you to pause there, Witness. I want us to go step-by-step. First of all, I would like to ask you the following: Where were you and the people you were with exactly positioned in this wooded area, in order for the Trial Chamber to understand?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was right above Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From that particular vantage point, were you able to see what was happening in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe what you saw, that is what was going on on the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th of April from the direction of Sase, Potocari, Zelani-Jadar, Skelani, Bjogare [phoen], rivers of vehicles with Serbs in them approached and entered the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time did you observe any of the SDS leaders there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Goran Zekic, who wore an officer's JNA uniform and was at the head of the column.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the direction from which the column was coming that he was heading?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please briefly tell the Trial Chamber what happened next in Srebrenica in the days to follow.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Looting, destruction, theft, murders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any women left behind there?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All the women who happened to be there were raped or killed or murdered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have the usher's assistance in showing the witness a document. This is a document from the Drina Corps archives headed "Report," dated 17 September 1992, bearing the following number: 03588224. The title of the document, the full title is "Report about the war booty and other goods from the territory of Srebrenica municipality." I will quote from the first paragraph and also a small portion from the second paragraph. "When Srebrenica and Potocarska Rijeka were liberated, enormous quantities of material assets and basic resources were seized. A large quantity of acids used in the floatation for led, zinc and silver separation was transferred from Potocari to the Veliki Majdan company in Ljubovija. Also, large quantities of explosives, detonator caps and fuses, a trailer truck loaded with tyres of various sizes, two trailer trucks and two buses, several freight vehicles and cars, truck number 2226, which transported items belonging to Miodrag Jokic and whose trailer was in the compound of the Trans Ljubovija company had been stolen. "The items driven away include a total of eight to ten buses, seven truck trailers, about 30 freight vehicles of the Transport Company from Potocari, and several dump trucks of the former construction company from Srebrenica, one cement mixer truck, and many other lorries, buses and cars that have remained remained in Serbia," and so on. I will move on to read the following: "I suggest that the MUP of the Serbian republic take urgent measures in order to prevent further looting and misappropriation of war booty." Do you agree with me that the last sentence I read out to you indicates to you that this source of the document is Serb, since it is proposed that the Serb MUP take measures?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This report on war booty and other properties, does it not reflect what you saw as having taken place in Srebrenica at the time, looting and taking away of property?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be assigned a Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let us assign an exhibit number to the map first. The map which was previously made use of will become Defence Exhibit D964. And this document that the witness has just testified upon with ERN 03588224, the Serbo-Croat version, two pages in English is being marked as Defence Exhibit D965.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that from the woods where you were hiding you were able to observe the situation in Srebrenica. Who were the attackers on Srebrenica on the 17th of April, 1992? Were they local Serbs or some outsiders?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: They were local Serbs from Sase, Zalazje, Bjogare, Orahovica, Podravanje and, in particular, from Skelani. I knew some of them who were there, because I got to know them as I was doing my fieldwork as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there some other people among them?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were those wearing different kind of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did the Muslims return to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: After Goran Zekic's death on the 7th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that some of them were wearing a different kind of uniform. The attackers that you mentioned came from those Serb villages, were they wearing uniforms or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of uniform did they have?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Olive-drab uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the other ones?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you returned to Srebrenica right after the 7th of May, 1992, or on that date. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the Serbs had withdrawn from Srebrenica, did they leave the inhabitants of Srebrenica and of the villages surrounding Srebrenica to live there in peace or did they do something else?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, they did not leave them in peace. They continued with intense infantry and artillery attacks against all the areas gravitating towards Srebrenica, all the villages and hamlets.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they shelling Srebrenica itself in?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us the exact period during which Srebrenica and Muslim villages were under these attacks?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: These attacks started on the 17th of April, 1992, and continued through to the demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have the usher's assistance now in showing the witness D731.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the command of the brigade of the autonomous region of Birac. Dated 31st of May, 1992, bearing the following number: 04276217. I will quote from a part of the document. "Pursuant to the decision of the government of the Serb autonomous region of Birac, therefore the Serb autonomous region of Birac, which regular rates the moving out of the Muslim population from the territory of the Serb autonomous region of Birac, I hereby order: "Set up a camp in Vlasenica and secure it in compliance with international regulations." My question to you is as follows: Based on your experience and on the experience of the refugees you spoke to, can you tell us whether this decision issued by the Birac government regulating the moving out of the Muslim population in the area of Birac was implemented? Does it not show that they wanted the entire Muslim population to move out of the area?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were able to see that. It was all planned and coordinated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show the witness a different Defence exhibit, D815.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document is by the Birac Brigade command dated 17 June 1992, bearing the number 04337554. Witness, take a look at the document before you. I will quote item 2, which says: "It is necessary that you urgently resolve the issue of prisoner's camps because we currently have 640 prisoners in Vlasenica." My question to you is the following one: In the context of the expulsions you mentioned, were you aware of a camp existing in the area of Birac?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Susica, also the one at Vlasenica, at Gradina, at Sase, at the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac, at the Jedinstvo stadium also in Bratunac. Many people lost their lives there and went missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you were aware of the intention of the Serbs to cleanse the area of Podrinje of the Muslim population. Were you aware of the fact that the local Serb population was assisted, helped by volunteers? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You therefore knew about it?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the reputation enjoyed by volunteers among the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: These were people from Serbia who had experience on the Croatian battlefield, and their one and only purpose was to kill.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown D832, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at page 01297987. That's the last page of the document. The title there is the testimony of a killer, but I will not read this article out to you. I will ask you the following: Is it not true that I showed you the article and that you carefully read the entire article?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now quote a small portion of the article that I intend to put a question on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in English it's page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I will quote the part starting as follows: What exactly was your task? What was actually your task. And the person interviewed gives the following answer: "The fifteen of us, volunteers from Vranje and the surrounding area were stationed in Fakovici. We undertook actions from there with local inhabitants who used to come from Bratunac. Muslim villages were up there in the hills, and we cleansed them one by one." "You say that you went into action. What do you mean by that?" "When we went into action, all the volunteers who were accommodated in Serb villages gathered there. Special units came from Bratunac consisting of people from the area who knew the terrain. The task of these people was to disable Muslim guards around the villages before the attack. During that time, we surrounded them and started with the attack at dawn. We burned everything that was in our path, threw bombs onto houses, opened fire. We captured a number of Muslims and sent them over to Bratunac. After our actions, villages were completely destroyed. Zanjevo, Tegare and seven or eight other villages. According to my assessment, about 4.000 to 5.000 Muslims were killed. Only in the forest in the village of Tegare more than 1.000 people were killed in three to four hours only. "Who did you fight against? Against the Muslim army? "No, they were civilians, villagers in most case insufficiently armed with double-barrelled guns and similar rifles." Witness, in interview given by Slobodan Misic he stated that in the events in which he participated after their actions, Zanjevo, Tegare and seven to eight villages were razed to the ground. Based on your knowledge, is it true that in the period from mid-April 1992 through to October 1992 the Muslim villages in the area around Fakovici, including Zanjevo, Tegare were destroyed in fact or not?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which were the villages that were destroyed? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Those were the villages of Zanjevo, Tegare, Donje and Gornja Orlica, Zapolje, part of Sikiric Rijeka, or rather the Muslim part of Sikiric Rijeka, Biljaca, Zaluzje, Voljevica, all these villages were destroyed in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as Tegare itself is concerned, it is stated here that in one day or, rather, in three or four hours more than 1.000 people were killed. My question is as follows: Do you know what happened in Tegare around mid-September 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Tegare was partially burned in early May so that the population from the village and the surrounding area fled to the woods in the area there. In early September, they returned to their village. To be more precise, on the 14th of September, in the early morning hours, Serb soldiers encircled the general area of Tegare and Fakovici, including the woods where large groups of refugees were hiding from -- those were refugees from the area of Visegrad who had managed to pull through through the Drina canyon on found refuge there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what happened that day?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, the Serb army encircled the area, the area including all the refugees there, and proceeded to kill whoever was alive. They took younger women and girls to the nearby woods, raped and subsequently murdered them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this point I would kindly ask us to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us, you said you had two sources. What was the other source?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: The other source of my information were the people who brought her. They also came to visit her aunt, and I spoke to them as well. What they had seen was a real massacre. When they arrived in the area of Tegare, they saw a child whose body was dismembered with a Zolja and a man whose body was placed in a basket and whose head was hanging out of this basket, whose mother had been slain. And there were two underaged children, bodies of two underaged children lying next to her. Apparently they had been shot from the back. Old people, whoever wore jewellery, their fingers had been cut off. The people in the area, in the area of Tegare, were simply massacred, whoever happened to be in the vicinity and in the woods surrounding the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The people with how many spoke at the time, did they tell you whether they knew who the perpetrators were?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: It was the girl who told me that, because she had gone to school to Fakovici, and she knew the people from Fakovici. But she also said that there had been people who spoke in Ekavian dialect who used abusive language and shouted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show to the witness a new document, which bears the number 04337115. It's a telegram which was sent to Milici on the 14th of September, 1992 to the command of the Birac Brigade. It was sent from Milici.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The telegram was sent from Milici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could I kindly ask you to have a look at it text which states as follows: "We are passing on to you a telegram from Gigant." And it goes on: "Our air force has been trained and is ready to be deployed in any task. We bombed Srebrenica with the approval of PANOS-5. "We will continue our attacks east of Srebrenica today. "Please forward your requests a day before. The moving of the Repovac-Magasici line to the LAD line was carried out, elevation point 408, Bresenjak, and 932." And now please pay attention to the last sentence: "Tegare completely liberated." Witness, my question in relation to this is the following: What town in Podrinje had air force?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've seen the last sentence of this document which says: Tegare completely liberated." Based on your knowledge, on the 14th of September, 1992, and around that day, was Srebrenica bombed from the area east of -- east of the town?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me go back once again to this last sentence. "Tegare completely liberated." The date is the 14th of September, 1992. Does this accord with your recollection of the time at the time you heard about the plight of the civilians, including the plight of this young girl whom you saw at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document, Madam Vidovic, will become Defence Exhibit D966.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown another document, please. It is another document from the Drina Corps command dated the 9th of January, 1992, number 04929466. It says "Very urgent. "To the Bratunac Brigade command (to the commander and Colonel Pritojevic)." And it goes on: "Participation of a group of 'Volunteers' in the zone of responsibility of the brigade." I'm not going to ask you about the time framework but about the phenomenon of volunteers and will you please pay attention to that. I will quote the first and the last paragraphs of this document. The first one: "We have received information about the arrival of a group of 'volunteers' of unknown numerical strength which is to take part in combat operations in the zone of responsibility of our brigade." And the last paragraph: "Do not, under any circumstances, engage this group along the axes where Serbian villages are located, and specifically relay this to the commander of the group." How do you understand this ban to engage the group of volunteers in the area of Serb villages, the order issued by Colonel Milenko Jovanovic [as interpreted], and how does this correspond to the information, to your knowledge, of the volunteers?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: It simply means that we're talking about very cruel, brutal people, unscrupulous people who would have no qualms about endangering even the Serb population in the areas they pass through.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you conclude personally that Colonel Jovanovic was aware of their cruelty at the time he sent them to the Muslim villages and banning them from entering Serb villages. Was he aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was referring to Colonel Milenko Zivanovic for the sake of the record, not Jovanovic. The commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for pointing that out, Ms. Vidovic, and it will be taken account of in the final transcript, I hope.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be given a Defence exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic. It has already become Defence Exhibit D967.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have told us that Serbs had mounted a severe attack and carried out a massacre in Tegare, in the area of Tegare that is. What I would like to know is whether the area of Srebrenica and the surrounding villages, in late September, early October 1992, were also under the pressure of the Serb forces or not.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were many artillery attacks, attacks from the air, infantry attacks. The encirclement was getting tighter every day, and they were trying to create an enclave out of Srebrenica. They were turning small villages into even smaller enclaves in order to force the population who was in the area because they lacked food and medicine to parish.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown a new document at this point, please. It is a document issued by the command of the Birac Brigade, a document by the Birac Brigade command dated 11 October 1992. The document bears the number 04337513. It is a daily operations report sent to the command of the Eastern Bosnian Corps, and it bears the name of Svetozar Andric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will quote just one sentence from this document. It's to be found under item 3 -- actually, I'm going to quote the item 3 of the document: "Situation in the area of responsibility: We are setting up ambushes. Our artillery is firing along the Caparde-Kalesija line." In connection with this, let me ask you a question and then I will move on with the document. This line, this axis Caparde-Kalesija, is this the route to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge, were there any ambushes as described in the document along that line, along that axis?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the road that the Muslims took on their way to Tuzla when they were attempting a breakthrough to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me continue with the document. "From the Bratunac side, the Voljevica-Pobrdje-Andrici line was moved and we're linking up with the forces from Sase, thereby considerably shortening the front line on that side. We are also moving the Bratunac-Glogova line to the positions on Kaolin-Ladja, elevation point 408 Vresje, point 3.532. We did not move the line held by the Kravica forces towards Konjevic Polje and they are still at Sopotnik-Lupoglava-Banjevici-Gornja Brana-Donja Brana-Neradje-Krusik-Marici-Lazarici-Menjak-Jezestica. "The Vlasenica PB forces are along the Potanjik Jasikovaca Nisava-Metaljka line. We have planned for the air force to launch an attack during the day against the forces intervening from Srebrenica. Combat operations have slowed down a little because of weather conditions. The situation at Crni Vrh - regular." Let me ask you the following: This document, Witness, does it confirm the situation as it was on the ground at the time when this document was created, that is the 11th of October, 1992? Is it true that Serb forces were linking up in the field and encircling Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Konjevic Polje, Srebrenica, and the villages around Srebrenica were all getting encircled at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become Defence Exhibit D968.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw in the previous document that it was dated the 11th of October, 1992. Do you remember, Witness, the month of October 1992? Was that the time of very intensive attacks on the enclaves of Srebrenica and Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those were the most severe attacks, artillery attacks, air attacks, and infantry attacks as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Defence exhibit -- a new Defence exhibit, which bears the number 01081631. It is a document issued by the War Presidency of the municipality of Srebrenica, and it bears the date of the 13th of October, 1992. It is -- it's title is "Appeal." And it says -- let me just read out a brief -- a small portion of the document. It states as follows: "Everything that has been happening in the last few days on the territory of Srebrenica, Konjevic Polje, and Cerska, as well as throughout the free territory in the region is worse than hell. "The SDS extremists are attempt to go destroy everything that can be destroyed with heavy artillery and with infantry attacks." Witness, let me ask you the following question: This document, does it reflect the actual situation with respect to the attacks against Srebrenica, Konjevic Polje, Cerska in the month of October 1992.

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it does. Those were extremely severe attacks, and the fall of Srebrenica was imminent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can I ask you if you remember which villages in the area of Srebrenica came under the attack of the Serb forces at that time, that is in October 1992. When were those attacks particularly intensive if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. On the 7th or the 8th of October the attacks were the most severe. 1992, of course. The villages of Potocari, Budak, Dugo Polje, Gogaze [phoen], Peceste, Likara [phoen], Isanik [phoen] came under a very severe attack from the direction of Bratunac and Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how long those intensive attacks were at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUAD SMAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. They lasted until the 13th or the 14th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document be given a number. I don't know, Your Honour, perhaps this is the time that you had in mind. Do you want me to stop with my examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will become Defence Exhibit D969. If you can finish the next point within, say, five minutes, then, yes, go ahead. Five minutes or so, plus or minus. I'm trying -- you know, I've made calculations between now and Friday how much time we have, give and take one hour, so go ahead for the next five, seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd rather stop at this point because I have to move to another subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Certainly, Ms. Vidovic. So, sir, we'll stop here for today. We will continue tomorrow in the afternoon at 2.15. You will now be looked after, taken back to your hotel. And please remember what I told you. Do not communicate with anyone on the matters related to your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm clear on that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, let's not waste time or lose time. Mr. Wubben, your final submissions on you know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will take the opportunity to make two submissions, Your Honour. First one will be an oral submission in reply to the response filed today in the way of a reply by the Defence today in written form, so this will be an oral reply. And the second will be an oral submission on the procedural matter referring to Rule 73. The reply by the Defence refers to a conclusion that as the Prosecution has submitted in the Rule 70 witness case that it may have contact with that witness but that the Defence request the Trial Chamber to rule on the contrary. That's the first request. And the second request is that the Prosecution may not have such contact in the absence of the Defence, particularly when -- while the response to the matters raised in ex parte Annexes A and B are still pending. Well, my reply are without any knowledge of the ex parte Annexes A and B, and I refer to the knowledge of this Bench to decide upon that. I will give my reply in the form of comments and refer to the particular paragraphs, Your Honour, starting with paragraph 2 in which paragraph the Defence refer to the information given by the Prosecution in the evening of Tuesday, the 29th of November, 2005, that it would be interviewing the witness, and that that information had the very unfortunate consequence of leading the Defence to believe that the Trial Chamber has rendered and entirely ex parte decision. Your Honours, that conclusion is -- has been made by the Defence. I refer to the reply already, the written reply, response by the Prosecution in that respect. The information that I provide to Defence counsel was that we will contact witness -- the witness tomorrow and that we will put questions to him and that I referred to both the order by the Trial Chamber and the right that each party has to interview witnesses, and I reiterated that limited statement twice though I was interrupted various times by another Defence counsel. Paragraph 4 is referring to the case law including various decisions by Chamber and appeal decisions. Those decisions, Your Honour, are all triggered by the very fact that witnesses were reluctant to testify and there had been a request for a subpoena for other way of dealing with compelling witnesses to testify or refrain to do so. I refer to the various rulings by that. That's another issue, the very fact that has been decided upon by the Mrksic appeal, which is that every party has a right to interview witnesses and that no party owns or sees a witness as a property -- as its property. Paragraph 6 is referring to an Article 18 of the Statute used by -- in the response by the Prosecution. I also refer in that field to Article 16 of the Statute that the Prosecution by itself is not limited only to investigation but encompasses also the execution of its role at the trial. Paragraph 7 of the reply by the Defence referred to a -- and I quote: "Cardinal reason for the principle that there is no property in a witness, and that is that until a witness is on the witness list for one party or the other, it remains for the other party to call that person as a witness." I see no argumentation in that because this issue, the very issue is not related to this case as it is not a matter of putting a witness on a list but the very right to interview that witness on behalf of cross-examination. Then it is stated in the same paragraph that as of argumentation that the testimony of this witness is scheduled in less than one week. This completely removes, and I quote, "any argument based on the possibility that the Prosecution might itself decide to call -- to call a witness." Well, in my opinion, that is not applicable as the Rule 70 provider as well as the witness already agreed to the planned interview by the Prosecution. Paragraph 9 is referring to the Halilovic appeals decision that -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I wish you to be very clear on this. I'll read what I have in the transcript and then I'll ask you a question, Mr. Wubben. "Then it is stated in the same paragraph that as of arugmentation that the testimony of this witness is scheduled in less than one week, this completely removes, and I quote, 'any argument based on the possibility that the Prosecution might itself decide to call -- to call a witness.' Well, in my opinion, this is not applicable as the Rule 70 provides [sic] as well as the witness already agreed to the planned interview by the Prosecution." Has the witness agreed, or has the US government or authorities agreed to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- to make it possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We ask for permission to interview the witness through the US government. The US government confirmed that we are allowed to give this interview. So I take it that is more indirectly. That's why I'm grateful for the question that I take it that the witness indeed agreed with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You agree with me -- I'm asking you a question. You're concluding from that that the witness has agreed to be interviewed by you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Through the organisation, and we discussed a time, the appropriate time to organise the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Eser would like to intervene at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Since I have some problems to understand paragraph 7, could you perhaps give your interpretation of it when it says: "Moreover, the testimony is set for less than one week. This completely removes any outcome, and based on the possibility that the Prosecution might itself decide to call Dudley as a witness." Perhaps the Defence may later on explain what they are meaning with the sentence, but what would be your interpretation of this sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My interpretation, because out of the fact that it is less than a week, that should conclude for the Prosecution that we might decide to call him as a witness, perhaps in rebuttal or something like that. I don't see it as an argumentation, because it has already been organised as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for your explanation. Of course the Defence has reserved the right to counter to that if they so desire. Let's go -- please proceed, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Paragraph 10 there is a reference to the fact that there is no investigative purpose behind the Prosecution request for contact with the witness, and according, I quote Your Honour, to the Halilovic appeals decision. "This is an insufficient reason to grant the request." Well, I read Halilovic appeals decision, and it is -- has to do again with the subpoena, but then also whenever you decide, whenever a Trial Chamber decides for a subpoena, it just -- it is not an easy instrument to do. It has to serve a certain purpose. Well, even for a subpoena it would serve a purpose because we were limited on our cross-examination, and this is how we try to get our full right, and that's also according, when the Defence counsel referred to Rule 20, that's completely in line with Rule 20, Your Honour. Paragraph 11 that's referring to the final travel plans having been made and a proofing schedule drawn up. That can also be no argumentation. As such, a travel plan and such a proofing schedule did not refrain the US government and nor - and that's indirectly a conclusion - the witness to agree 10 days before travelling to The Hague, or around 10 days, to allow such an interview and didn't stop them to allow that as such. The -- in paragraph 15 and 16, the Defence refer to the Stanisic Trial Chamber decision that there should be a consent by a witness, and I again reiterate that not only already consent has been given but indeed explicitly by the US government and we confirmed that several times who deals with the US government with its party separately when it comes to Rule 70. So there is no need for the Defence in such a manner as addressed in paragraph 16 to consider that it would be given the opportunity to contact the witness and to ask whether or not he consented to the contact -- contact with the opposing party as I can now refer to an explicit letter in that regard. I come to an end of my first oral submission, Your Honour. There is a reference to the concerns of leaking of ex parte material elicited by the Defence. I refer to the letter by the US government of the 2nd of December in which by the end it is reiterated that such questions are not allowed. The US government deals with each party separately. So also related in paragraph 18, the danger that this may reveal the ex parte content of the Prosecution interview with the witness. That's only the case if the Defence itself requests for such an information, but I believe that the Defence will never do so, Your Honour. In paragraph 19, there's a reference that Prosecution might obtain authorisation -- might have obtained authorisation to raise other matter with the witness and that's unclear to the Defence whether this include permission to raise those matter in cross-examination. This is also answered in the second-to-last paragraph of the letter of the 2nd of December. I refer to that letter due to the time limits. Also, when it comes to the second part of it, I quote: "It will be necessary for the Prosecution to disclose the additional matters." The additional matters, that's in the same way as also the Defence stated and argued in the initial Defence motion for a Rule 70 ruling stating by the ex parte filing of all these issues these are protected by Rule 70. So also the Prosecution is bound to that. That's why -- that's why, Your Honours, it still remains for me as a conclusion that the Prosecution should respectfully request a dismissal of the Defence motion seeking to bar the Prosecution from conducting an interview of this witness. The Defence in their reply, in its reply also refers to an a clarification sent to the -- as a request to the US government, we cannot wait for it, and that's why I have a short, limited oral submission, Your Honours. If I may proceed on a procedural matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Referring to Rule 73 in the case that this Trial Chamber deny the motion by the Defence. So in that case, we noticed that the Rule 70 witness is scheduled for the 12th to the 14th of December, meaning that's from Monday. So he will be proofed in the prior days, presumably the weekend. The Defence might further clarify. That leaves us for tomorrow and Thursday as this witness should then depart from the US on Friday. Subsequently, we have to set up a correspondence with the US government for authorisation and would like to inform Trial Chamber as well, to notify you of such authorisation. That means for me a request, an urgent request for a ruling on this motion as early as Your Honours are possible to do so, and if so, preferably tomorrow morning, so that we can address the issue of organising such an interview. Again, in the case that -- that the Trial Chamber denied the motion by the Defence, to enable such an interview by Thursday. But, Your Honour, it's also now already at a late stage, and so far, and we tried also this afternoon, we couldn't get guarantee that -- this is possible, as we have to contact again after we voluntarily rescheduled the earlier organised interview by -- by last Wednesday, the 30th of November. And that's all due to the motion by the Defence asking to reschedule it. Now, the request to the Trial Chamber is an order -- an order for an adjournment or delay of the scheduled testimony by the Defence of this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know who is dealing with this. I presume -- yes. Judge Brydensholt would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to raise a question towards the Prosecution, because as I see it now at least, the problem for the Defence seems to be that the interview should be in the absence of the Defence, and that is the whole question of ambush and all that. I haven't heard the argument. Why is it that the Prosecution is against that the Defence is present without any right to interrupt but just to be aware what's going on? Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you for asking, because it is not a matter of being blunt to the Defence in that respect. It's a matter of the same reason why parties do not invite other party, opposing parties, to their interview. They want to define their own strategy. They want to have the right and to feel free to ask questions about anything, and it's the same as the Defence did not invite also this very Prosecution to their witness. But apart from that -- apart from that, we want to execute this right for -- for a witness interview by ourselves. And I would like also to refer to apart from that as a third argument to the letter by the Rule 70 provider, the US government, on the 2nd of December in which it explicitly clarifies and confirms that there is an isolated approach when it comes to parties and dealing with the witness that has the label of Rule 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, firstly, Your Honour, on that last point I know that that's a woefully inadequate response. It doesn't address the question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, before you start, do you have a reply from Mr. Jones with regard to the letter that you filed which is dated today? In other words, is your witness prepared to give -- allow himself to be interviewed by the Prosecution and particularly is he allowed to -- is he prepared to allow himself to be interviewed by the Prosecution in your absence? Or when I saw "your absence," I mean a representative of the Defence. Because the United States government cannot decide for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. May I come to that, Your Honour. There are two issues with the United States government, and in order to first be clear on all the issues, it's easiest if I address what Mr. Wubben said a moment ago. To me, first of all, when the Prosecution first sought to argue that the United States government is opposed to us being present at the interview, I thought that that was bound to be wrong, that that was obviously strange. I phoned the US embassy last Friday and said surely the intelligent, reasonable way to understand your letter is that you're saying we don't on our own initiative tell the other party what is happening, but they don't have a position as to whether we're there or not, and the fact that the Prosecution wants to rely on the US government that they're the ones saying we're not to be present it shows the total absence of any argument on their part, and I'll read right now I have an e-mail from the US government, and I trust that when Mr. Wubben sees that's the position, since that's the only argument, that he will then agree that certainly, if Your Honours were to allow contact, that we should be present because there is no basis on the part of any US government opposition, and in this regard I'll waive the ex parte nature of Annex B. I wrote to Mr. Johnson and said could they confirm in writing that as I understand it, the USG does not itself have any objection to both the Prosecution and the Defence being present at any interview of LTC Dudley if the parties so agree or the Trial Chamber so orders. The UGS's position, as I understand it, is simply that you will not inform either party when the other party conducts such an interview. That's my message. An e-mail which I received today: "Dear John" - this is from Heather Schildge - "we will be sending you a response to your letter imminently. As I told you by phone, your understanding is correct, and we will confirm this in writing. We were not able to respond earlier today as we were in a lengthy meeting." So that's -- as far as that is concerned, I think really the Prosecution, if they were being open and fair about this, they wouldn't to put it on the US government, that it's the US government who doesn't want us on to be present. They have no position on that matter. Now, as far as the submissions of Mr. Wubben are concerned, and they're lengthy, but I'll deal with them as quickly as possible. It's very important, Your Honour, that I have a right to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You will have every opportunity to do that, Mr. Jones. But I am more interested in your letter to Heather, which presumably was sent today, this morning, Tuesday, 6 December, in which you ask the embassy basically to possibly transmit a message to Colonel Dudley and advise him of your normal practice to advise all witnesses that you intend to call that should the Prosecution wish to contact them, then they should request that the Defence be present too and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. The reasons are important --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has this been done to your knowledge and do they have a feedback?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour is reading from ex parte annex, but again this was done in a hurry, and I'm happy for the interest of moving on with this, the Prosecution hasn't made their ex parte annexes inter partes, but I'm happy unless I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to redact and we go into private session, I'm prepared to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. No. Just in abundance of caution this morning, I kept my correspondence ex parte, and the Prosecution's correspondence with the USG are all ex parte, but I think it helps to -- to look at that. Yes, indeed, our normal practice is to -- is to advise witnesses that if the Prosecution should wish to contact them, then the Defence be present too, in order to ensure full transparency, equality of arms, and protection of the interests of the accused, as well to ensure that there are no misunderstandings between us and the witness at a later stage when the witness comes to The Hague for proofing and testifying, which I trust you'll see is a reasonable position. And on that matter, the answer is: "Regarding the other message from Mr. Dudley as a USG witness, all communications with him will go through the USG," and so basically we're waiting for a response on that matter. And I'll deal with both those points in sequence, but I think it's first important to clear -- to clear those up. Now, the thing which I find most galling, I have to say, about Mr. Wubben's reply is that he said it's due to us, due to our urgent motion that now we're in a terrible rush. Well, the Prosecution has had years, years to make contact with Mr. Dudley. They've certainly had months since we've listed him as a witness to make contact with him. They told us at the absolute last possible moment when we say it was so that we would not be able to actually do anything about it that they were going to interview him, but it didn't stop there.
